newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chip companies drive Moroccan bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip companies drive Moroccan bourse lower.

text.p: Casablanca stock market closed on Monday slightly lower mainly due to stagnation of blue chips and a drop in share value of Societe Nationale d'Investissement, brokers said.
The all-share index dropped 0.08 percent to 427.24 points from Friday's session.
SNI, which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 companies and has a market capitalisation of more than 5.7 billion dirhams, lost two dirhams to close at 578 dirhams.

"The bourse index drop is considered by traders as a noraml correction...We expect the market to resume its upward trend as soon as local mutual funds return to the market," Jalal Houti, a Casablanca-based stockbroker, said.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, Morocco's second largest bank, remained stable at 660 dirhams.
ONA Group, the country's largest private conglomerate, was unchanged at 460 dirhams.
Wafabank, and Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, market blue chips, remained unchanged respectively at 500 and 405 dirhams.
The most marked change was registered by Credit Eqdom, which rose 29 dirhams to close at 1,029 dirhams.

Eqdom said on Monday it was to increase its capital to 166.6 million ($19.1 million) from 111.1 million dirhams. It said the capital would be increased in two simultaneous operations of a stock split and a rights issue.
The traded volume was not available.
